_meta.source: shipbuilder/tools/game_logic_notes.md, Finding 13 (Rockwood Nut), Finding 14 (Spacekorn), Finding 16 (continuous gate-checking/death-timer/Invasive-spread), Finding 17 (quantity-vs-speed attr semantics), Finding 18 (dial mechanics + the exact harvest-yield formula) and Finding 19 (a neighbor's adjacency effects run for its whole post-germination lifetime, not just while still growing) - decompiled from data.cdb sheet 'farm' and ent.b.Farm/ent.b.PlotZone (src/ent/b/Farm.hx: updatePlots/checkProgress/applyPlant/hasMinRequirement/getEnrichmentValue/serverRegularUpdate/setDeployInfo and ent.SpaceBase.gatherPlant__impl). Hand-transcribed, not script-regenerated - if game_logic_notes.md gets a new/corrected finding for these crops, update this file to match.
_meta.mechanism: The Xenic Farm building has one shared Temperature dial (Cold/Temperate/Warm/Hot) and one shared Light dial (UV/Natural/Dark) - a single farm is never in two temperature or light states at once. Each grown variant's gate is a set of acceptable dial positions (OR-across-allowed-states); a variant with an empty temperature/light list is unconstrained (any dial position satisfies it) - EXCEPT a variant marked 'unreachable: true' (see that field's own note below), whose empty list means the exact opposite. After germination, ALL variants whose gates currently pass become candidates and the game picks uniformly at random among them (not priority order) - if none pass, the plant dies instead of stalling.
_meta.growth_death_mechanism: Requirements are checked continuously, not just once - letting fertilizer, dial position, or a neighbor restriction go unmet stalls growth and starts a 5-hour death countdown (fully recoverable if restored in time; the countdown also winds back down while requirements are met). The farm being unpowered or disabled fails EVERY plant's requirements at once - and its dials snap back to the planet's ambient positions until power returns. Water is a hard requirement that can never be waived (even by Rockwood Dream's neighbor tolerance). Once a plant reaches its final harvest stage, requirements stop mattering entirely. Every adjacent EMPTY plot also gives a plant +5% Growth & Production speed (harvest-neutral, see the harvest note) - a fully-packed grid grows slightly slower per-plant than a checkerboard.
_meta.adjacency_timing: Verified 2026-07-26 (Finding 19, raw disassembly of updatePlots): a neighbor's OWN growth stage never gates whether its adjacency effects reach you - only which row currently occupies its plot does. A germinating seed gives nothing yet (no grown-variant row assigned, so no adjacency data exists to read). The instant that seed resolves into a grown variant, that variant's adjacency list is live - active from the start of its own growth, not deferred until it's fully grown. It keeps applying all the way through full maturity while sitting unharvested at the gather stage, since nothing in this code path distinguishes 'still growing' from 'done growing, awaiting harvest' - only dying (progress swaps the plot to a separate deadVariant row) stops it. Practically: a companion pairing (Green/White + Woolly, White + Bitter, Plain + Sour, etc.) does not need its two crops harvested in lockstep to keep the bonus flowing - the companion buffs its neighbor for its entire post-germination lifetime, right up until it's actually picked or dies. A mature, UNHARVESTED plant can even be parked as a static 'battery' next to a crop its own dial would normally conflict with (grow Woolly to maturity under Cold, then swap the farm to Warm and grow Sour beside it - the parked Woolly no longer cares about the dial once mature, and keeps handing out its +20% Byproduct quantity regardless).
_meta.dream_tolerance: Verified 2026-07-27 (Finding 20, raw disassembly + Finding 13's own allowMissing description reread more carefully): Rockwood Dream's adjacency effect ('neighbor tolerates 1 unmet requirement') is the only allowMissing grant anywhere in this dataset, and it doesn't just delay a neighbor's death timer - hasMinRequirement's own pass condition is missingCount <= allowMissing, so a covered miss makes the gate PASS, meaning growth continues normally with one requirement genuinely wrong. Combined with adjacency_timing above (a live, un-parked Dream works fine - no parking needed), this means a Dream neighbor can let a plant grow on a farm dial that doesn't match its own gate at all, PROVIDED exactly one of the five checked things (fertilizer-required / fertilizer-forbidden / temperature / light / no-restricted-neighbor-tag) is what's wrong - a second simultaneous miss still fails (confirmed already for Rockwood Glow, which needs two waived and can't get them - Finding 13's own loophole-ruled-out note). Two real consequences, both re-verified against the actual formula, not just the mechanic in isolation: (1) FERTILIZER-SKIPPING, zero downside: Green can skip Neutral Fertilizer, White can skip Metallic, Bitter can skip BOTH Acidic and Metallic at once (missing either or both of a required list is still just one 'fertilizer-required' miss, not one per item) - none of these three items carry an enrichment of their own, so skipping them (once tolerated) costs nothing. Two adjacent Dream plants can even waive each other's Elmerium Dust the same way, PROVIDED each one had it at the exact moment its own germination resolved (the tolerance is 'gated on non-seed stages' per Finding 13 - a germinating seed's own variant-selection roll doesn't get it, so the real fertilizer must be present for that one moment, and can be pulled immediately after). (2) DIAL-MISMATCH GROWTH, real but rarely worth it: Bitter/Plain/Sour can each grow on Dream's Cold-or-Temperate-or-Warm+Dark dial via a Dream neighbor even where their own gate would normally exclude that temperature - but doing so forfeits their OWN dial-triggered enrichment (Bitter's Hot-only Byproduct+40%, Plain's Temperate-only speed), so per-plant output is always worse than their own dedicated Vault. The one exception is Woolly specifically: under Warm/Hot/Temperate, Woolly needs Dream's tolerance just to grow at all (Cold has zero overlap with anything else), making a live, fully-sustainable Dream+Woolly weave a genuine alternative to Layout G for players who want both products from one farm - not a per-plant win, a diversity option, same caveat as Layout D-mix. One further, sharper case: under COLD specifically (Woolly's own native dial, needing no tolerance for temperature at all), Woolly's one tolerance slot is free to cover a DIFFERENT miss instead - its own 'no Putrescent neighbor' restriction - letting it sit directly next to Sour or Bitter and hand over its +20% Byproduct quantity live, no parking required. Verified per-plant numbers for this: White gains a Bitter neighbor's Putrescent-mult trade AND a Woolly neighbor's quantity bonus simultaneously (both fit on one plot without conflicting, since neither is Reclusive/Putrescent to the other) - harvest byproduct 152 -> 166 (+9%); Sour gains a Woolly neighbor the same way - harvest byproduct 20 -> 22 (+10%). NEITHER is reflected in goal_presets: both require sacrificing real plot space to Dream and Woolly cells that would otherwise be more White/Sour, and per_slot_vs_per_farm above already demonstrated on Plain that a smaller-but-boosted plot count usually loses the farm total outright once counted - these two cases have not been re-verified at the full-grid level the way Plain's was (the tiling constraint-satisfaction problem, fitting enough Dream+Woolly coverage to enhance most or all of a variant's plots while keeping Reclusive/Putrescent restrictions intact across a 15-cell grid, was judged too easy to get subtly wrong by hand and was not attempted). Treat these two numbers as verified-per-plot, NOT verified-per-farm, and not in-game tested at all - logically derived from Findings 13/16/18/19/20 together, not independently re-checked against fresh disassembly the way each of those individually was.
_meta.harvest_mechanism: Corrected 2026-07-25 (Finding 18): fruit and byproduct are NOT repeating post-maturity drips. Both accumulate invisibly WHILE the plant grows (only during ticks its requirements pass - stalled time contributes nothing) and pay out ONCE, in a single lump sum, when the mature plant is harvested - after which the plot resets to empty and needs replanting. 'fruit_cycle_hours'/'byproduct_cycle_hours' below are the game's real per-item timers (each rolled once per planting, uniform in its range): the harvest yields ceil(accumulated_hours / per_item_hours) of each product. With no modifiers, accumulated hours = the growth duration, so base yield per harvest = growth_hours / cycle_hours (e.g. Spacekorn Plain: 36-40h growth, 4-6h per Plain Pulp = roughly 6-10 Pulp per harvest). Exact game formula: yield = ceil(growth_duration * (1 + quantity_bonuses) / (per_item_duration * productive_metabolic_speed)) - see _meta.effects for how each modifier slots in.
_meta.dial_mechanics: Verified from raw disassembly (Finding 18): dial changes take effect INSTANTLY (next server tick) while the farm is powered - there is no transition/ramp time. The four Temperature positions are the same canonical targets on every planet; only their power cost differs (30 power per 'step' of distance from the planet's ambient band - the position nearest ambient is free, e.g. Temperate is free on a Temperate planet, Cold is free on a Frozen one, Warm is free on a Hot planet). The UV light position costs a flat 20 power; Natural and Dark are free. A farm deployed at a spot with no natural light (the game checks the deploy site's light level) has NO Natural position at all - selecting it just sets Dark; only UV lamps or Dark are possible there. When unpowered, both dials snap to the ambient defaults (nearest-ambient temperature; Natural if the site is lit, else Dark) and every plant stalls regardless (see growth_death_mechanism). A neighboring Rockwood Glow forces a plot to be treated as UV-lit for ALL light checks - bonuses AND requirements (it would e.g. break a Dark-requiring plant's gate) - replacing, not stacking with, the farm's actual light dial.
_meta.enrichment_trigger: An enrichment entry's optional 'trigger' field ({kind: 'temp'|'light'|'neighbor_tag', values: [...]}) marks the ones frontend/js/farming.js can render as a pill instead of plain text: 'temp'/'light' are gated by the SAME shared Temperature/Light dial as the variant's own grow-gate, rendered as the same dial chips used in Requirements; 'neighbor_tag' names a bio-tag (see each variant's own 'bio_tag' and 'neighbor_restriction_tag') a neighbor plant must carry, rendered as the same pill used for the bio-tag badge and the Requirements Neighbor line. Fertilizer conditions carry no trigger - there's no established pill style for those. A neighbor_effects entry (as opposed to an enrichment) carries a different trigger kind, 'neighbor_variant' ({kind: 'neighbor_variant', values: [variant id, ...]}) - added 2026-07-27 alongside the exact-grid-search pass (see _meta.exact_grid_search) so a specific-neighbor bonus (Plain's own 'plain_neighbor', or any 'woolly_neighbor'/'glow_neighbor' entry) can be resolved against a real grid's actual neighbor identity without parsing the free-text 'label' - the previous label-matching approach had a real bug (matching on a shared crop-family word like 'Rockwood', not the specific variant), fixed by adding this field to every existing neighbor_effects entry rather than trying to make text-matching more clever.
_meta.unreachable: A variant's optional 'unreachable: true' (+ 'unreachable_note', the player-facing explanation frontend/js/farming.js shows in a warning banner) means its grow-gate can NEVER pass in normal play, confirmed by both raw disassembly and a direct in-game test - it is not just rare or hard, it's a dead branch of pickVariant. Only Rockwood Glow (Glowwood) is marked this way: its 'temperature'/'light' fields are present with a literal integer 0 in the source data rather than being absent, and hasMinRequirement only skips the dial check on an ABSENT field - a present 0 always fails the bitwise-AND test, every tick, no matter the farm's dial position. This is the opposite of every other 'unconstrained' variant in Findings 13/14 (which all use an absent key), so Glowwood's empty temperature/light arrays here do NOT mean 'any dial position works' the way they do for other variants - see this field's own presence as the disambiguator, and always check it before treating an empty temperature/light list as unconstrained. A theorized loophole (stacking Dreamwood neighbors' allowMissing tolerance to cover both misses) was investigated and ruled out - it caps at 1, Glow needs 2. The only way to place it at all is a debug/admin-only function, not normal play.
_meta.fertilizer_forbidden_any_removed: An earlier revision marked Rockwood Glow 'fertilizer_forbidden_any: true' (no fertilizer of ANY kind may be present) based on a live-play impression, explicitly flagged for follow-up against raw disassembly. That follow-up happened (2026-07-25, Finding 18): the game's requirement checker has no such branch at all - a variant can only require or forbid SPECIFIC supplements, and Glowwood's game-data gate carries neither list. The flag was wrong and has been removed; Glowwood's fertilizer cell is simply unconstrained (academic anyway, since its temperature/light gate is unreachable - see 'unreachable').
_meta.effects: Replaces the earlier 'speed_effect' model (2026-07-25, Findings 17/18) - the old model treated fruit/byproduct numbers as cycle TIMES, which the game does not do (see harvest_mechanism). An enrichment's or neighbor_effect's optional 'effects' array ([{attr, value}]) uses the game's own attribute semantics: 'all_speed' (additive; speeds growth AND product accumulation equally - harvest comes sooner, yield per harvest UNCHANGED - the game calls it Growth and Production Speed), 'growth_speed_mult' (multiplicative on growth progress only - the game's Productive Metabolic Speed; a value below 1 grows SLOWER but yields MORE per harvest by exactly 1/value, since products keep accumulating over the longer growth - the game's own description spells out this tradeoff), 'fruit_qty' / 'byproduct_qty' (additive quantity bonuses: multiply that product's yield by (1+sum), no effect on any time). Frontend math (all verified against the disassembled formulas): growth_time = growth_hours / ((1+sum all_speed) * (1+sum growth_speed... there is no additive growth_speed in current data) * product growth_speed_mult); fruit_yield = ceil(growth_hours * (1+sum fruit_qty) / (fruit_cycle_hours * product growth_speed_mult)); byproduct likewise. Note all_speed cancels out of the yield formulas entirely. Entries sharing a 'dial_group' (temp/light) are mutually exclusive in the UI (the farm holds one Temperature and one Light position at a time); entries with no dial_group toggle independently. neighbor_effects entries carry the same 'effects' array plus their own 'effect' prose line, rendered identically to enrichment rows (condition -> effect) so no toggle is ever description-less. Either kind of entry may also carry an 'effect_note': a longer aside (dead-code caveats, stacking rules, the why behind a slower-but-richer tradeoff) shown as a hover tooltip on the effect text rather than inline - keep 'effect' itself to one readable line; a long inline effect used to wrap onto its own full-width line, visually detaching from its row. The game data also defines multiplicative fruit/byproduct-quantity attrs, but they are DEAD CODE in the current build (computed then discarded, confirmed at raw-opcode level) - the one place they appear (Spacekorn's UV entry, a would-be -20% byproduct malus) is described in prose but carries no effect entry. Every togglable entry (any enrichment or neighbor_effect carrying 'effects') also carries a stable 'id', added so per-variant 'goal_presets' below can reference exactly which toggles a recommended setup implies without duplicating numbers - the id is a slug, unique within that variant, not global.
_meta.goal_presets_and_layouts: Added alongside the Layouts reference view (frontend/js/farming.js): each variant's 'goal_presets' names, for each of the 'rate' (items/hour) and 'harvest' (items/harvest) framings, which of that SAME variant's own toggle ids to check for an 'overall' (both products), 'fruit_only', or 'byproduct_only' goal - deliberately not precomputed numbers, so the Layouts view drives the exact same live calculator as the Reference view and can never drift from it. A goal's preset always includes every toggle genuinely part of that setup (including pure-speed ones), not just the ones touching the target product - the only toggles ever dropped for a *_only goal are fertilizer-only bonuses that contribute nothing to the wanted product, since spending a supplement slot for zero benefit is waste, not a neutral choice (a bonus that's free either way - i.e. costs no fertilizer, most neighbor effects - is always kept). The {no_dominant: true, options: [...]} shape (for a genuine Pareto trade-off with no single winner) exists in the schema but is deliberately UNUSED: it was tried for real on 2026-07-27 as a way to represent 'overall' whenever fruit-optimal and byproduct-optimal genuinely diverge (a 2-option menu re-presenting the fruit_only/byproduct_only answers side by side), then abandoned the same day once it was clear that doesn't actually answer 'what's best if I want both' - see _meta.exact_grid_search for what replaced it (a genuine combined-objective search that resolves 'overall' to one real answer every time). Each preset also names a 'layout' (a key into the top-level 'layouts' object) - most variants use the same layout across every framing/goal (Green, Dream, Bitter, Sour, Woolly), Plain and White both fork fruit_only/byproduct_only by which product is the goal but NOT 'overall', which always names its own single combined-optimal setup (see their own goal_presets and _meta.exact_grid_search). Discovered while building the ORIGINAL version of this view: Rockwood Green, White, and Dream were all missing a 'Neighboring Woolly Spacekorn' neighbor_effect - Woolly's own +20% Byproduct quantity to 'any neighbor' (see ChillyEinkorn's adjacency line) had only ever been recorded as what Woolly does to others, never mirrored onto the receiving variants' own cards the way Rockwood Glow's UV-lit effect already was - so it was real but untoggleable. Fixed then since it directly changed which pairing was optimal for White; fixed AGAIN for Bitter, Plain, and Sour on 2026-07-27 when the exact-grid-search work below made clear the same gap existed for every variant a parked/battery Woolly could reach, not just the three that can live alongside it.
_meta.exact_grid_search: 2026-07-27: the entire goal_presets/layouts dataset was re-derived by an exact, exhaustive search (a Python column-by-column dynamic program over the 3x5 grid, covering every dial position x fertilizer subset x grid placement combination - including PARKED/battery neighbors per Finding 19/20, not just live ones) rather than the hand geometry that had produced every layout before this pass. The search itself isn't checked into this repo (a scratch tool, not app code) - what follows is what it found, each cross-checked against the app's own live formula before being written back here. Three real bugs were caught and fixed WHILE BUILDING the search itself, worth recording since they're easy to reintroduce: (1) matching 'is this neighbor_effects entry a same-species bonus' on a single shared name-word false-positived for any two variants sharing a crop-family word ('Rockwood', 'Spacekorn') - e.g. Sulfwood's own glow_neighbor entry ('Neighboring Rockwood Glow...') wrongly matched Sulfwood's OWN name ('Rockwood Bitter') on the word 'Rockwood' alone, silently granting every solid-packed Bitter cell a phantom free UV-lit bonus; fixed by matching on the FULL display name instead (see the same fix applied to the app's own neighbor_variant trigger, _meta.enrichment_trigger). (2) a variant's neighbor_restriction_tag (Reclusive for Green/White/Glow, Putrescent for Woolly) was initially not modeled as a hard constraint at all, producing an ILLEGAL 'solid pack' answer for Green/White (two Reclusive cells can never be mutually adjacent - checked continuously per growth_death_mechanism AND at the moment a fresh seed resolves into that variant per mechanism, so no planting order or parking trick ever gets around it, unlike case 3 below) - fixed by excluding any grid arrangement where an ACTIVELY-GROWING/replanted cell has a same-restricted-tag neighbor. (3) the opposite mistake was then made correcting (2): a BATTERY cell's own restriction was, briefly, ALSO checked against its current neighbors - wrong, since growth_death_mechanism's 'once a plant reaches final harvest stage, requirements stop mattering entirely' applies to a battery's OWN restriction too, not just its dial/fertilizer gate (this is exactly what already lets a parked Woolly sit next to Putrescent-tagged Bitter/Sour despite Woolly's own live gate forbidding it) - fixed by only ever checking a restriction against the cell that's actively, continuously growing, never against an already-parked one. Findings, variant by variant: GREEN's existing Layout B checkerboard was already exactly optimal (unaffected by any of the three bugs above, since its illegal-solid-pack candidate was never actually superior even before the constraint was fixed... it was just never legal to compare against in the first place). WHITE's Layout C had a real, independent bug (unrelated to the three above): its checkerboard coloring had White in the 7-cell MINORITY instead of the 8-cell majority, losing 12.5% of achievable harvest for nothing; fixed, AND upgraded to mix in Woolly alongside Bitter (previously not considered together) - since a White plot only needs ONE Putrescent-tagged neighbor for Bitter's full metabolic-slowdown trade (non-stacking), spending the REST of its neighbor slots on Woolly instead of a second redundant Bitter is free extra Byproduct on top. The corrected Layout C is now simultaneously optimal for fruit harvest, byproduct harvest, AND byproduct rate - only fruit rate still wants the old all-Woolly Layout C-alt instead, a genuine (small) difference on the rate table. PLAIN's Layout D was already byproduct-optimal on both framings (confirmed, not just assumed, by the exact search - no battery placement ever beats a full 15-plot vault there), but fruit-focused goals were leaving real value on the table: a sparse, 2-cell parked-Sour battery (Layout D-sparse) lifts fruit harvest 60 -> 66 (+10%) for free (no dial cost, since it's a pure quantity bonus), and a 3-cell version under a live Temperate+UV dial (Layout D-sparse-rate) lifts fruit rate 4.53 -> 4.98/hr (+10%) WITHOUT losing Temperate's own speed bonus - previously assumed impossible, since a LIVE Sour forces Warm and forfeits Temperate outright (Layout D-mix's actual problem). Both cost real byproduct (2-3 fewer Plain plots), so fruit_only and byproduct_only genuinely differ by layout for Plain now - not the false trade-off D vs D-mix used to model on the rate table specifically (_meta.per_slot_vs_per_farm), a real one the earlier hand-geometry pass never found because it never tried a SPARSE, non-uniform placement at all. A THIRD pass, run once fruit_only and byproduct_only stopped sharing a layout for the first time (Plain and White both), asked what 'overall' should mean now that a single re-used layout+toggle union no longer answers it: rather than present the two single-metric extremes as a menu (tried briefly, see goal_presets_and_layouts), 'overall' is resolved by maximizing a genuine COMBINED objective - each product's total normalized against its own independently-best achievable value (from the first pass) and summed 1:1, then the full dial x fertilizer x grid search is re-run end to end against that combined score. Results: White's rate 'overall' lands on Layout C-alt (same as fruit_only) with Neutral Fertilizer added on top - free byproduct, since Neutral never touches fruit_qty; White's harvest 'overall' was already covered by Layout C's simultaneous dominance above. Plain's rate and harvest 'overall' BOTH land on Layout D-sparse plus Neutral Fertilizer - the same setup for both framings, unlike fruit_only/byproduct_only which still differ (Plain's own goal_presets merge rate/harvest 'overall' into one panel again, same as every non-forking variant). A third, distinct 2-cell Sour placement was found during this pass and then deliberately NOT kept as a separate layout once cross-checked: it tied Layout D-sparse's own combined score exactly (both cover 7 of Plain's 13 non-battery cells - coverage COUNT is what determines the total here, not which specific cells), so it added a redundant near-duplicate layout for zero real benefit. DREAM, BITTER, and SOUR were all re-confirmed exactly optimal as already documented, including 'overall' (the combined search found their existing single shared layout already achieves the maximum possible combined score - both products simultaneously at their own individual best) - in particular, Bitter's and Sour's own woolly_neighbor entries are real and toggleable (a parked Woolly CAN legally sit beside either, per bug (3) above) but the exact search confirms it's simply never worth the lost plot for either of them; their solid Vaults remain correct with no caveat. WOOLLY was unaffected (it has no usable battery source of its own). This pass also required a schema/frontend change beyond the JSON alone: goal_presets' existing 'layout + blanket toggle_ids' shape assumes every counted cell shares an identical neighbor profile, true for every checkerboard/solid layout that existed before this pass but NOT true for Layout D-sparse/D-sparse-rate's non-uniform battery coverage - frontend/js/farming.js's farm-total box (renderFarmTotalBox) was rewritten to sum each matching cell's OWN per-cell adjacency (collectEffectsForCell/gridNeighborCells) instead of multiplying one blanket accumulator by a count; verified to give identical answers to the old shortcut on every uniform-coverage layout, so nothing else needed to change. One more gap surfaced once the layouts actually shipped: nothing distinguished a companion cell that grows LIVE, in place, alongside the target (Layout B's Woolly, Layout D-mix's Sour) from one that can only ever be a PARKED battery under that layout's own dial (Layout C's Woolly, Layout D-sparse/D-sparse-rate's Sour) - the board just showed both as an ordinary occupied cell. Fixed without a new data field: frontend/js/farming.js's isLiveCompatibleWithDial derives it straight from the occupying variant's own temperature/light gate against the layout's own dial (empty gate = unconstrained = always compatible; the layout's own target cells never land in this set, since the dial was chosen to suit them) - a mismatch means that cell can only be there already mature and deliberately left unharvested. Surfaced three ways: a dashed accent outline + small corner badge on the board cell itself, a '⏸ parked' pill in the legend row, and a standalone callout on the card (naming which variant(s) and reiterating the grow-elsewhere-first requirement) whenever a preset's own layout has at least one such cell.
_meta.one_way_neighbor_pairings: Corrected 2026-07-27: three checkerboard/weave layouts (B, C, D-mix) pair a Reclusive-or-lonely variant (Green, White, Plain) with a companion (Woolly, Bitter/Sour, Sour respectively - see fertilizer_scope for why Layout C's own companion later changed from Bitter to Sour) that genuinely helps it - but the companion's own goal_presets had wrongly pointed back at that SAME shared layout, implying the pairing helps both sides equally. It doesn't: Bitter's own perk (-50% neighbor supplement consumption) and Green's own perk (neighbor SEED germination/death-timer speed) aren't among the four attrs (all_speed/growth_speed_mult/fruit_qty/byproduct_qty) this app's calculator tracks at all, and Sour has no neighbor_tag enrichment of its own to receive anything through in the first place - so Bitter, Woolly, and Sour each get nothing measurable back from their half of the pairing. Layouts E/E-alt (Bitter), F (Sour), and G (Woolly) are solid monocultures added so each variant's OWN goal_presets recommend packing every plot with itself (more total plants, since the companion crop was doing nothing for it) rather than wasting half the farm on a neighbor it doesn't benefit from. The paired layouts (B/C/C-alt/D-mix) remain correct - they're just the answer for the BENEFICIARY (Green/White/Plain), not the companion. One theoretically-real pairing that still can't happen: Woolly's blanket byproduct bonus is crop-agnostic, so it would help Sour too if they were neighbors - but Sour's gate (Warm/Hot) and Woolly's gate (Cold only) can never both be satisfied by one farm's single shared Temperature dial, same conflict that already rules out Bitter+Woolly living together (Bitter's own woolly_neighbor toggle is battery-only for exactly this reason).
_meta.fertilizer_scope: Per the player (2026-07-27), not yet independently verified against decompilation the way the rest of this file is (flagged here the same way the 'up to 3 supplements' cap already was, back in Finding 13): the real Xenic Farm building is FOUR separate 3x5 plot groups, each with its OWN independent fertilizer loadout, sharing only the farm's single Temperature/Light dial across all four. CraftMap's own 'layout' grid (always 3x5) models exactly ONE such group, so this doesn't change the scale of anything already in this file - a goal_preset's own 15-cell grid IS a real, complete fertilizer-sharing unit, not a quarter of one. What it DOES mean: two LIVE (not parked/battery - see adjacency_timing) variants sharing one of these 15-cell groups also share one fertilizer loadout, so a layout mixing two live variants is only achievable if neither's fertilizer_forbidden list intersects the other's fertilizer_required/optional choices. This was checked for every current goal_preset (only one violation found and fixed, see Layout C's own note - Bitter's own forbidden Carbonic conflicted with White's own optional Carbonic bonus, swapped for Sour instead, identical numbers, no conflict) - every other DECLARED live-live pairing in this dataset (Layout B: Green+Woolly, Layout C-alt: White+Woolly) already has compatible fertilizer needs. A PARKED/battery companion is exempt from this entirely, same as every other one of its own requirements (growth_death_mechanism) - only two LIVE, currently-growing variants sharing a group can conflict this way. This check alone isn't the whole story, though - see _meta.germination_ambiguity for a related, more fundamental issue it led to finding: even a layout with only ONE intended variant can have an UNDECLARED same-crop sibling whose gate also happens to pass, with no forbidden-item conflict involved at all.
_meta.germination_ambiguity: Discovered 2026-07-27, prompted directly by the player questioning whether a layout was actually achievable: 'After germination, ALL variants whose gates currently pass become candidates and the game picks uniformly at random among them' (mechanism, Finding 13) applies per INDIVIDUAL PLOT/SEED, not per intended layout - and per the player, only a CROP ('species' - Rockwood Nut vs Spacekorn) has its own distinct seed item; there is no variant-specific seed that could force a specific grown result. So whenever a layout's own dial+fertilizer setup happens to ALSO satisfy a different variant of the SAME crop (not just the one the grid says should be there), a seed planted in that plot has a real, non-zero chance of becoming that other variant instead - regardless of which cell the grid claims it occupies. This is a strictly different failure mode from fertilizer_scope's own cross-variant forbidden-item conflicts (which block growth outright, deterministically) - this one lets growth SUCCEED, just as the wrong variant, some fraction of the time. Checked exhaustively for every crop's own variant (temperature x light x every achievable fertilizer subset, not just this file's own current layouts) using a from-scratch brute-force script (not checked into this repo): Rockwood Green/White/Dream and every Spacekorn variant (Plain/Sour/Woolly) each have AT LEAST ONE clean (unambiguous) dial+fertilizer combination achievable - Rockwood Bitter does NOT, under ANY combination. Bitter requires Acidic AND Metallic Fertilizer simultaneously plus a Warm/Hot dial; White's own gate (unconstrained dial, only needs that same Metallic, forbids nothing at all) is satisfied by every single one of those environments with no possible exception - there is no fertilizer item Bitter could add or dial position it could pick that excludes White, since White has no forbidden list to violate and no dial constraint to fail. This reads as a genuine, permanent property of the game's own data (not a CraftMap authoring gap) - Layout E/E-alt's own notes and Sulfwood's own goal_preset_note both carry this caveat now: there is no way to grow a farm group of pure Bitter, full stop. Every currently-ACTIVE goal_preset besides Bitter's own Vault was re-checked against its OWN real fertilizer set (target's required + optional-toggled items, plus every other live companion's own required items) and found clean, with one exception that WAS fixable: Layout F (Sour Vault) used to list Warm as equally valid alongside Hot, but Warm is also inside Plainkorn's own accepted range and Plain has no fertilizer requirement to exclude via Sour's own Carbonic - so Warm let Plain sprout there too. Fixed by dropping Warm (Hot alone excludes both Plain and Woolly, at zero cost to Sour's own numbers - it has no temperature-triggered enrichment). One more consequence, arguably the most important: Layout D-mix's own deterministic-looking Plain/Sour checkerboard turns out to be UNACHIEVABLE by live, simultaneous growing at all - under its own Warm dial, Plain's gate and Sour's gate both pass at literally every cell (same root cause as Layout F's bug, just uncorrectable here since the whole point is having BOTH present), so the real result is an uncontrolled random blend, not the clean alternating pattern the grid draws. This retroactively validates why Layouts D-sparse/D-sparse-rate's parking-based technique (found independently by exact_grid_search, for numeric reasons) is not just numerically better than D-mix but the ONLY mechanically real way to deterministically combine Plain and Sour on one farm group - grow the Sour cells first under a dial that excludes Plain (Hot, not Warm - see those layouts' own notes), let them mature, and only then switch the group's dial for Plain's own growing phase.
_meta.per_slot_vs_per_farm: Corrected 2026-07-27, superseding the reasoning (not the conclusions) in one_way_neighbor_pairings above. Every goal_preset here is chosen by FARM TOTAL - per-plant yield multiplied by how many plots of that variant the layout's own grid actually contains - not by per-plant yield alone. The two aren't the same thing whenever the candidate layouts differ in plot count, and trusting per-plant numbers alone produced one real wrong answer before this pass: Spacekorn Plain's rate table was documented as a genuine Pareto trade-off between Layout D (monoculture, 15 plots) and Layout D-mix (Sour-neighbor stripe, 9 plots) - D-mix's per-plant numbers ARE individually higher (0.349 vs 0.302 fruit/hr, 1.105 vs 1.207 byproduct/hr - byproduct was already D's per-plant win, fruit wasn't). But farm totals tell a different story on every axis: fruit 4.53/hr (D) vs 3.14/hr (D-mix), byproduct 18.1/hr (D) vs 9.95/hr (D-mix), fruit harvest 60 vs 54, byproduct harvest 240 vs 171. D-mix's 9-plot ceiling loses to D's 15-plot ceiling every time, once counted - there was never a real trade-off, only a per-plot one. Plain's goal_presets now point at Layout D universally; the no_dominant shape that used to model this trade-off is unused but kept in the schema (see goal_presets_and_layouts). Every other variant's assignment was re-checked the same way and already held: White has no monoculture alternative to compare against (Reclusive forces the checkerboard), and for Dream/Bitter/Sour/Woolly, packing solid wins by such a wide margin (e.g. Dream: 15x50=750 vs an 8-Dream/7-Woolly checkerboard's 8x54=432, even though the checkerboard gives Dream a real +8% per-plant boost from a Woolly neighbor) that no layout in this dataset was close. The general rule this establishes: a per-plant improvement only matters if (new plot count / old plot count) x (new per-plant / old per-plant) > 1 - a large per-plant gain on a much smaller plot count almost never clears that bar in a 15-plot grid, which is why solid monocultures dominate this dataset's farm totals whenever they're mechanically available at all.

A.label: Dream Vault
A.note: Full pack, single variant - Dream carries no Reclusive/Putrescent tag and no neighbor restriction, so there's no conflict to route around.

B.label: Green / Woolly Weave
B.note: Green's own weave - every Green plot's neighbors are all Woolly, never another Reclusive plant, so this packs solid at 15/15 with no gate-failure risk, and Woolly's blanket byproduct bonus reaches every Green plot. Woolly itself gets nothing measurable back (Green's own perk only speeds up a neighbor's germination/death-timer while it's still a seed - not one of the four attributes CraftMap's calculator tracks) - it's grown here purely as Green's companion. If Woolly is the actual goal, see the Woolly Vault layout instead.

C.label: White / Sour+Woolly Mix
C.note: Corrected 2026-07-27 by exact grid search (color-assignment bug + missing Woolly mix), corrected AGAIN 2026-07-27 (fertilizer scope): the Putrescent-tag companion here was originally Bitter (Rockwood Bitter/Sulfwood), which also satisfies the tag and is also live-compatible with this dial - but Bitter's own fertilizer_forbidden list includes Carbonic Fertilizer, which this layout's own toggle set NEEDS present (White's own optional Carbonic bonus) for the numbers below. Fertilizer is shared per 3x5 plot group, not per individual plot (per the player, not yet independently verified by decompilation the way the rest of this file is) - so a live Bitter neighbor sharing this same group would make Carbonic Fertilizer's presence break ITS OWN forbidden-item gate continuously, which isn't an achievable setup at all, not just a suboptimal one. Sour (Spacekorn Sour/SourEinkorn) carries the same Putrescent tag, is equally live-compatible with this dial (its own gate is Warm/Hot too), and its OWN required fertilizer is Carbonic itself - no conflict, and the numbers are identical either way since the tag-based bonus doesn't care which specific Putrescent-tagged variant provides it. Filled by a MIX of Sour (4 cells) and Woolly (3 cells) rather than all-Sour: every White plot only needs ONE Putrescent-tagged neighbor to get the full metabolic-slowdown trade (non-stacking), so once that's covered, spending the REST of a plot's neighbor slots on Woolly instead of a second redundant Sour is free extra Byproduct quantity on top, for both of White's products at once - this one grid is simultaneously optimal for fruit harvest, byproduct harvest, AND byproduct rate - so it's also the harvest table's 'overall' answer outright, no trade-off at all there (see Whitewood's own goal_presets; only the rate table's fruit-rate/overall goals want a different, all-Woolly grid, see Layout C-alt). Sour itself gets nothing measurable back (it has no neighbor_tag enrichment of its own to receive anything through); Woolly likewise gets nothing back. Both are grown here purely as White's companions - see the Sour Vault/Woolly Vault layouts if either is the actual goal.

C-alt.label: White / Woolly Checkerboard
C-alt.note: White's fruit-rate-optimal pairing, and (with Neutral Fertilizer added on top) also the rate table's 'overall' answer - Woolly's blanket +20% Byproduct quantity with none of Bitter's metabolic slowdown, since fruit rate never wants a bigger-but-slower harvest. Corrected 2026-07-27: this used to also claim byproduct rate outright, but exact grid search found Layout C's mixed Bitter+Woolly grid actually wins byproduct rate once the slowdown's extra accumulated quantity is weighed against its speed cost (12.5/hr vs this layout's own best 8.4/hr) - so byproduct_only points at Layout C instead (see Whitewood's own goal_presets). A combined-objective search (maximizing fruit and byproduct rate together, each normalized against its own achievable best) confirmed this layout is still the right call for 'overall' too, not a compromise pick - adding Neutral Fertilizer (free: it only touches byproduct_qty, never fruit) closes most of the byproduct gap without giving up any fruit rate at all, landing closer to Layout C's own byproduct number than the fruit-only setup's plain 8.4/hr.

D.label: Plain Vault
D.note: Plain's own byproduct-optimal setup on both framings, and still the fruit-byproduct-balanced choice for 'overall'. Per-plant, D-mix's Sour-neighbor quantity bonus individually beats this on fruit rate and on harvest size - but D-mix only fits 9 Plain plots to this layout's 15, and that plot-count gap outweighs the per-plant edge on every single metric once you total the farm (see farming.json's own _meta.per_slot_vs_per_farm for the worked numbers). A different, sparser technique (2-3 parked Sour 'battery' cells, Layouts D-sparse/D-sparse-rate) DOES genuinely beat this layout on fruit-focused goals specifically - see Plain's own goal_presets. Grow Sour separately (Layout F) if you want its own byproduct too - mixing a live Sour crop in via D-mix costs Plain more than that pairing ever gives back.

D-sparse.label: Plain Vault + 2 Sour Battery
D-sparse.note: Added 2026-07-27 by exact grid search - found only once the search covered PARKED (not just live) neighbors: 2 Sour cells, deliberately grown to maturity earlier and left unharvested (Finding 19/20's parking technique), placed so between them they touch every OTHER cell in the grid. Bumps fruit harvest from Layout D's 60 to 66 (+10%) for free - no dial cost at all, since the Putrescent quantity bonus needs no particular Temperature/Light position. Costs 2 Plain plots' worth of Plain Pulp (byproduct harvest 240 -> 229, -4.6%), so it's not a strict upgrade over Layout D - see Plain's own goal_presets for when fruit_only/byproduct_only genuinely diverge. Harvest 'overall' also lands on this exact grid (Neutral Fertilizer added, since it's free byproduct on top with no fruit cost) - a separate combined-objective search confirmed it, not just fruit_only's own preference carried over by default. IMPORTANT sequencing note (see _meta.germination_ambiguity): grow the 2 Sour cells FIRST, under Hot specifically (not Warm) - Warm is also inside Plainkorn's own accepted range, so a Spacekorn seed planted under Warm here risks becoming Plain instead of the intended Sour battery; Hot excludes Plain entirely. Only switch the group's dial to this layout's own Temperate afterward, once the Sour cells are already mature and parked (a mature plant's own gate stops being re-checked at all, so the later dial switch doesn't affect it).

D-sparse-rate.label: Plain Vault + 3 Sour Battery
D-sparse-rate.note: Added 2026-07-27 by exact grid search, same parking technique as Layout D-sparse but one more battery cell (3, not 2) since items/hour rewards covering more plots more than items/harvest does. Bumps fruit rate from Layout D's 4.53/hr to 4.98/hr (+10%) WITHOUT losing Temperate's own speed bonus (the parked Sour is immune to the farm's live dial once mature) - previously assumed impossible, since a LIVE Sour forces Warm and forfeits Temperate entirely (see Layout D-mix). Costs 3 Plain plots' worth of Plain Pulp (byproduct rate 18.1/hr -> 16.5/hr), so it's the right call for rate's fruit_only specifically, not for 'overall' - a combined-objective search found rate 'overall' actually prefers Layout D-sparse's own 2-cell placement instead (ties exactly: both 2-cell arrangements cover 7 of Plain's 13 non-battery cells, and coverage COUNT is all that determines the total here, not which specific cells). Same sequencing requirement as Layout D-sparse (see _meta.germination_ambiguity): grow the 3 Sour cells under Hot, not Warm, before switching the group's dial to Temperate for Plain - Warm would risk Plain contaminating the battery cells themselves.

D-mix.label: Plain / Sour Stripe
D-mix.note: Not farm-total-optimal for EITHER crop grown here (Plain's own per-plant numbers are higher than in Layout D, but D fits 15 Plain to this layout's 9 and wins the farm total regardless - see Layout D's own note and _meta.per_slot_vs_per_farm; Sour gets nothing measurable from Plain either and has its own farm-total-dominant monoculture, Layout F). MORE IMPORTANTLY (added 2026-07-27, see _meta.germination_ambiguity): the deterministic alternating pattern shown here is NOT actually achievable by live, simultaneous growing - under this layout's own Warm dial, Plainkorn's gate and SourEinkorn's gate BOTH pass at every single cell (Plain has no fertilizer requirement of its own to exclude via the Carbonic Fertilizer Sour needs), so a Spacekorn seed planted anywhere in this group has a real, roughly-random chance of becoming either one - not the controlled 9/6 split drawn here. Layouts D-sparse/D-sparse-rate are the actual working way to combine Plain and Sour deterministically on one farm group (grow Sour first under Hot, which excludes Plain entirely, then switch the group's dial to Temperate and plant Plain in the remaining cells - the already-mature Sour keeps its bonus regardless once parked, Finding 19/20). This layout is kept as real, verifiable data (the grid IS a legal state to end up in, just not a controllable one) - not as an achievable recommendation.

E.label: Bitter Vault
E.note: Bitter's own harvest-optimal setup. Bitter gets nothing measurable back from a companion neighbor, so a solid monoculture beats any checkerboard pairing for Bitter's own total output - same plant count doing useful work either way, but here every plot is Bitter instead of half going to a companion crop Bitter doesn't benefit from. (Bitter was briefly White's own Layout C companion too, until a 2026-07-27 fertilizer-scope correction swapped it for Sour there - see Layout C's own note; this Vault was never affected either way.) IMPORTANT (see _meta.germination_ambiguity): unlike every other Vault in this file, this one can NEVER be grown as pure Bitter - Rockwood White's own gate (unconstrained dial, needs only Metallic Fertilizer, forbids nothing) always ALSO passes wherever Bitter's does, since Bitter needs that same Metallic plus Acidic. There is no dial or fertilizer choice that excludes White here; expect a real, roughly-random fraction of these plots to sprout White instead of Bitter, with no known way around it.

E-alt.label: Bitter Vault (UV)
E-alt.note: Bitter's own rate-optimal setup - same monoculture as Layout E, UV instead of Dark since UV wins on speed with no yield tradeoff (see Bitter's own Light-dial fork). Only the dial differs from Layout E; the grid is identical. Same caveat as Layout E applies here too, unaffected by the Dark/UV choice: this can never be grown as pure Bitter, since Rockwood White's own gate always also passes wherever Bitter's does (see _meta.germination_ambiguity).

F.label: Sour Vault
F.note: Sour's own setup, all goals and both framings - Sour has no neighbor_tag enrichment of its own (its fruit and byproduct numbers never depend on what's next to it), so a solid monoculture beats the Layout D-mix stripe for Sour's own total output. Corrected 2026-07-27 (germination_ambiguity): this used to also list Warm as equally valid (no dial-triggered enrichment differs between them for Sour's OWN yield, which is still true) - but Warm is also inside Plainkorn's own accepted range, and Plain has no fertilizer requirement of its own to exclude via this layout's Carbonic Fertilizer, so a Spacekorn seed planted under Warm here has a real, roughly 50/50 chance of sprouting Plain instead of Sour. Hot excludes both Plain (needs Temperate or Warm) and Woolly (needs Cold), so it's the only one of Sour's two accepted temperatures that actually guarantees Sour - not just 'equally valid,' the only correct choice.

G.label: Woolly Vault
G.note: Woolly's own setup, all goals and both framings - Woolly has no neighbor_tag enrichment of its own, and Green's perk (the one thing a Layout B neighbor would give it) only ever touches a neighbor's transient seed-stage timers, not any of the four attributes this app tracks. A solid monoculture beats the Layout B weave for Woolly's own total output.
